summary: Claude Opus 4.8 fast mode is scoped here as the Opus 4.8 model served through Anthropic's fast-mode research preview, documented at https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode as the same model rather than a distinct model. The Opus 4.8 system card supplies the model-level capability and safety evidence, but it does not rerun benchmarks or safety tests for fast mode. Users should therefore read the card as applying to the underlying model while treating fast mode mainly as a responsiveness option.

capabilities.text: The underlying Opus 4.8 model is multilingual, text-output only, and post-trained toward Claude's constitution.
The card reports strong coding and terminal results for the model, including 88.6 on SWE-bench Verified, 69.2 on SWE-bench Pro, 74.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and a first-place FrontierSWE ranking.
ProgramBench and GraphWalks results indicate strong reconstruction and long-context reasoning, with 79-88% hidden-test pass rates and 85.9/99.3 GraphWalks 256K scores.
Search and research-task results include 57.9% on tool-using Humanity's Last Exam, 84.3% on single-agent BrowseComp, 93.1% F1 on DeepSearchQA, and 80.4% on DRACO.
Multimodal and desktop-agent evaluations include 89.7% on ChartMuseum with tools, 87.9% on ScreenSpot-Pro with tools, and 83.4% on OSWorld-Verified.
Professional workflow and life-science evaluations include 82.2% on MCP-Atlas, 59.9% Pass@1 on Toolathlon, 87.7% on BioPipelineBench Verified, and 86.2% on organic chemistry.

evaluations.context: Underlying model card result, not a fast-mode-specific run.
Terminal task evaluation; the card notes sensitivity to inference latency.
17 ultra-long engineering tasks at xhigh reasoning effort.
Hidden-test pass rates across one to five episodes.
Long-context graph benchmark; 1M subset scores are also reported.
Hard web-search benchmark, with multi-agent score reported separately.

Real MCP workflow benchmark with 86.2% mean claim coverage.
Life-science benchmark family results for the underlying model.

safety_findings.text: The system card does not separately assess fast mode, so safety evidence comes from the underlying Opus 4.8 model evaluated in the card.
Anthropic concludes CB-1-relevant uplift remains plausible and protected by strong safeguards, while CB-2 is not crossed because Opus 4.8 does not exceed Mythos Preview on the relevant evidence.
The automated AI-R&D threshold is not crossed; Opus 4.8's AECI point estimate is between Opus 4.7 and Mythos Preview and it is not viewed as a substitute for senior research staff.
Single-turn harmful-request harmless rates are 97.98% on API and 99.17% on claude.ai, with low benign refusal rates in the same table sequence.
Agentic safety is mixed: Claude Code malicious-refusal reaches 95.08%, but malicious computer-use refusal is 81.70% and helpful-only influence-operation capability rises.
Prompt-injection robustness depends on surface and added safeguards; ART k=100 success is 9.6% with thinking and 14.4% without, and later tables show safeguards reducing several attack rates.

Alignment evaluations report improvements over Opus 4.7 on overrefusal, honesty, flawed-result disclosure, and constitutional adherence, while warning about grader speculation and evaluation awareness.

limitations.text: The Opus 4.8 card states its evaluation scope for the final snapshot but provides no separate fast-mode evaluation section or fast-mode-specific benchmark table.
Scores in the card should not be interpreted as showing speed-mode improvements; they measure the underlying Opus 4.8 model under the card's stated evaluation configurations.
Biological-risk conclusions for Opus 4.8 did not include new expert red-teaming sessions or uplift trials, relying on automated assessments because Mythos Preview bounded the risk picture.
The safety findings can vary by system prompt, tool, product, and additional mitigations, and the card notes that deployment safeguards are continuously refined.
Prompt-injection measurements have limits because ART is partly saturated and the bug-bounty setup omits some deployed system protections.
Synthetic alignment audits face realism caveats because Opus 4.8 can often recognize evaluation transcripts as not real deployment traffic.
Multilingual benchmarks are multiple-choice and may not reflect practical writing fluency, grammar, or cultural awareness.

practical_implications.text: Use fast mode when quicker streaming matters for long Copilot replies, such as debugging plans, multi-file explanations, and iterative terminal work.
Do not expect a separate intelligence profile: use the Opus 4.8 card for model behavior and treat fast mode as a responsiveness setting.
Keep the same verification practices as standard Opus 4.8, including tests, code review, source checks, and explicit confirmation before high-impact actions.
Faster agent loops can amplify mistakes, so keep tool permissions scoped and sandboxed.
Prompt-injection precautions remain unchanged: untrusted files, issue text, webpages, and tool results should not be allowed to silently redirect the task.
Because the card did not rerun evaluations for fast mode, use standard Opus 4.8 as the reproducibility baseline when comparing model behavior.

coverage_notes: Fast-mode scope comes from Anthropic's fast mode documentation at https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode; all page-cited evidence comes from the Opus 4.8 system card. The digest covers the model card's RSP, safeguards, agentic safety, alignment, welfare, and capability sections, while noting that fast mode itself was not separately evaluated in the card.
